verdict.summary: PB Fintech scores 44/100 and fails the Trend Template on four counts (c2, c3, c4, c8) — 150 DMA below 200 DMA, 200 DMA falling, 50 DMA below the longer averages, and RS percentile only 46. Per Gate 1, this terminates actionable analysis regardless of the improving earnings trend. The stock is in a deep, prolonged base (48+ weeks, 30.9% depth) and is technically broken, not building strength. Fundamentally there are real positives (accelerating EPS, strong sales growth, margin expansion) but earnings quality is weak — other income is still a meaningful chunk of PBT in several recent quarters, cash conversion is poor (3-yr OCF/PAT negative), and FCF has been negative for 3 straight years. Verdict: Reject/Avoid until price reclaims the moving averages and RS improves.
strengths: EPS growth accelerating sharply over trailing quarters (52-164% YoY)
Sales growth consistent in the high-30s% YoY range with 28.7% 3-yr CAGR
Net margin expanding YoY (+233 bps) and operating margin trending up
Clean balance sheet: near-zero debt, 15.5x interest coverage, no pledge, minimal dilution
Institutional holding rising over last 4 quarters (70% to 78%)
weaknesses: Fails Trend Template on 4 of 8 criteria (150>200 DMA, 200 DMA slope, 50 DMA position, RS percentile) — Gate 1 failure, not investable per Minervini rules right now
RS percentile only 46 — well below the 70 minimum threshold
Other income has been a large share of PBT in several recent quarters (as high as 176%, still ~52% in latest) — earnings quality concern
3-yr OCF/PAT ratio negative (-0.12) and FCF negative in all 3 reported years — cash generation quality is poor despite reported profit growth
ROE (9.75%) and ROCE (10.3%) both below Minervini quality thresholds
Base depth of 30.9% over 48+ weeks reflects a stock still working through a large corrective structure, not a tight, mature VCP
verdict.biggest_risk: OTHER_INCOME_DRIVEN — reported earnings acceleration is partly inflated by non-operating other income rather than pure operating profit, undermining the reliability of the EPS growth story used to justify the fundamental score.
